prize_parts.citation: For the rational design and synthesis of molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pore architectures and active sites

statement.case_for: Zeolite and molecular-sieve design is the clearest case on the shortlist where atomic-level structure was deliberately engineered and then shown to explain function. Structure-directing agents, new framework types and site-controlled catalysts (Zones at Chevron, Davis in synthesis and structure-directing concepts, Corma in catalytic design) are confirmed by decades of independent work and are deployed at very large scale in refining, petrochemistry and emission control. Structural proof is not in doubt, because these frameworks were solved crystallographically, increasingly by electron diffraction for the nanocrystalline ones. The work is mature, a field I know well, and recognition is arguably overdue. It is also solidly chemistry, which neither of the two biology-adjacent leaders is clearly.
statement.case_against: The theme is broad and hard to cite sharply. Credit is spread over many groups (Yu, Tsapatsis, and earlier work by Barrer, Breck and Flanigen that is not on the list), and a three-person cap forces an arbitrary cut. It is also the only ballot on which I am the sole first-place voter, so the committee may reasonably read it as a field-specific preference of mine rather than a broad judgement. The opening ballots show real support for B007 and B061, which I should weigh seriously rather than dismiss because they lie outside my specialty.

responses.point: Induced-proximity degradation turned the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a designable chemical tool, and PROTACs and glues make undruggable proteins addressable. Aili would credit Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli.
responses.response: I agree this is a real conceptual advance and I ranked it fourth for that reason. My reservation is timing and attribution. Clinical benefit is still partial, with no approved PROTAC that I know of, so the evidence is less settled than for a mature field. PROTACs and glues are also separate strands: the cereblon work is a mechanism discovery for existing drugs, whereas PROTACs are rational design. A three-person list that merges them leaves out Handa, Ito, Sakamoto or Ciulli depending on the choice. I would support this ballot if the committee can settle that split. Today it looks less ready than the zeolite case.

responses.point: Chabes places B007 first, with Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explaining the glue-degrader mechanism alongside Crews and Deshaies.
responses.response: Including Handa is the better choice, because the cereblon identification is what is structurally and mechanistically verified, and ternary-complex structures back it up. That is the kind of evidence I look for. But it makes the prize a combination of a design concept and a target-identification discovery. A citation covering both has to be written carefully, or it becomes a list of two stories. I would also want to hear Andrei on whether degrader efficacy in patients is established well enough to call the field mature.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks base editing first and argues for crediting Liu alone, since it is a simple chemical idea (engineered deaminases on a programmable scaffold) with first clinical programs.
responses.response: The single-laureate story is clean, and I agree that the chemistry content in deaminase engineering and directed evolution is real. My qualification is that base editing builds on the CRISPR platform recognized in 2020, so the chemical novelty is the effector, not the targeting. The Nishida and Kondo priority question is also not settled. I ranked it seventh. It is a serious alternative, but I do not think it is more mature or more clearly chemistry than a designed catalyst class with decades of deployment.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, ranks massively parallel sequencing first as a chemistry-based measurement platform whose consequences are very large and mature, with credit to Balasubramanian, Klenerman and Rothberg.
responses.response: I accept the impact and the maturity, and the reversible-terminator chemistry is real. I did not rank it in my top eight, though, because I am not convinced the committee can credit a three-person subset fairly. Ju, Mayer and the cluster-amplification contributors are strong, and the Solexa and 454 lineages are different technologies. Impact alone does not decide scientific merit; the zeolite case has the same impact with a cleaner structure-to-function argument. If the committee does choose sequencing, I would want the citation anchored on the chemistry of the method.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling first as a ubiquitous, mechanism-guided molecule-making method, crediting Buchwald and Hartwig.
responses.response: This is a strong candidate that I did not rank. It is mature and its attribution is cleaner than for zeolites. I take Peter's point that C-N coupling is a distinct capability. My concern, which he also raises, is the overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and the Kosugi precursor. I do not think that overlap rules it out, and I would not oppose it. If forced to choose between established, mature catalysis options, I would still place designed porous catalysts ahead because they have no earlier prize in the area.

uncertainties: How to define the B013 achievement sharply enough for a prize citation, and whether Corma, Davis and Zones are the right three rather than Yu or Tsapatsis.
Whether B007 should be split between PROTAC design and cereblon or molecular-glue mechanism, and whether clinical evidence is sufficient yet.
Whether sequencing (B001) and base editing (B061) are judged as chemistry by the committee, and how much weight the 2020 CRISPR prize should carry for B061.
My industrial-impact claims for zeolite catalysts rest on general knowledge and are not verified from the supplied files.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. I work on zeolite and porous-framework structure determination by electron diffraction, which is close to B013 scientifically, and I know the field's community, but I have no stated personal or institutional tie to Corma, Davis or Zones. I flag the proximity so the committee can judge whether it matters.
